newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission to rule against Clabecq aid.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission to rule against Clabecq aid.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to rule next week that a 1.5-billion-Belgian-franc ($47 million) capital injection for steel maker Forges de Clabecq amounts to public subsidies and cannot be approved.

A Commission official said the draft decision concluded "unequivocally" that the capital injection by the Belgian region of Wallonia and other rescue measures represented state aid -- something the Belgian authorities have strongly contested.

The European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) bans subsidies to the steel industry as a general rule. Restructuring and other forms of aid can still be allowed, if submitted as such, by EU industry ministers acting unanimously.
But the Belgian authorities have always contested that the Clabecq plan involved subsidies.
The Commission had no choice but to say: "this amounts to subsidies and subsidies are prohibited under the ECSC treaty", the source told Reuters.
The same applied to the other rescue measures, the source said. They include a bridging loan of 200 million francs paid by the Societe Wallone de Siderurgie and the waiving of claims.
The Belgian authorities had given no indication as to whether they would re-submit the plan under article 95 of the treaty which allows for restructuring aid under strict conditions.
